html:
The Picts were the peoples of what is now Scotland north of the Firth of Forth in the early Middle Ages. They are on the map for 800 and 900, their last centuries.

Roman writers first used the name Picti, "painted people", in 297. The Picts were descended from the Iron Age tribes beyond Hadrian's Wall and spoke a Brittonic language. They left carved stones with symbols that no one can fully read. In 685 they beat the Northumbrians at Dun Nechtain and kept their independence. Monks from Iona made them Christian.

In 839 the Vikings killed a Pictish king and much of his nobility. Soon after, Cináed mac Ailpín, Kenneth MacAlpin, of the Gaelic kingdom of Dál Riata, became king of the Picts. By 900 their kingdom was called Alba, Gaelic replaced the Pictish language, and the Picts faded into Scotland.
